edges.cite: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2011 conceptual model (AD organized into views)
edges.note: An architecture description expresses the architecture as a set of one or more architecture views.

edges.cite: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2011 (a view is governed by exactly one viewpoint)
edges.note: Each view is constructed following the conventions of, and governed by, a single viewpoint.

edges.cite: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2011 (view comprises models of one or more model kinds)
edges.note: A view is composed of architecture models, each governed by a model kind.

edges.cite: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2011 (viewpoint establishes one or more model kinds)
edges.note: A viewpoint sets the conventions for a view by specifying its constituent model kinds.

edges.cite: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2011 (viewpoint frames one or more concerns)
edges.note: A viewpoint is defined to frame a specific set of stakeholder concerns.

edges.cite: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2011 (framework comprises viewpoints)
edges.note: An architecture framework packages a coordinated set of viewpoints.

edges.cite: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2011 (framework establishes model kinds)
edges.note: A framework's viewpoints carry the model kinds it prescribes for architecture description.

edges.cite: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2011 (framework identifies concerns)
edges.note: An architecture framework identifies the stakeholder concerns its viewpoints are meant to frame.

edges.cite: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2011 (AD identifies stakeholders and concerns)
edges.note: An AD identifies the concerns it must address to scope which viewpoints/views are needed.
An architecture description may be expressed using an ADL as its notation.
ADRs capture the decisions and rationale that accompany and justify an architecture description.
An ADR records the context and forces (concerns) driving one architecturally significant decision.
4+1 is a specific fixed set of viewpoints, i.e. a concrete architecture framework.

edges.cite: Kruchten, 'Architectural Blueprints—The 4+1 View Model', IEEE Software 1995
edges.note: 4+1 defines the logical, process, development and physical viewpoints plus scenarios.
The Rozanski-Woods catalog is a concrete framework packaging seven viewpoints.

edges.cite: Rozanski & Woods, Software Systems Architecture, viewpoint catalog
edges.note: The catalog enumerates seven reusable viewpoints (context, functional, information, ...).

edges.cite: Rozanski & Woods, Software Systems Architecture (viewpoints + perspectives)
edges.note: Rozanski-Woods pairs its viewpoint catalog with quality perspectives applied across views.

edges.cite: Rozanski & Woods, Software Systems Architecture (perspectives applied across views)
edges.note: A perspective is applied across an AD's views rather than forming a view of its own.
A perspective bundles tactics to ensure a particular quality-property concern holds.

edges.cite: Clements et al., Documenting Software Architectures (module viewtype)
edges.note: The module view is one of the three SEI viewtypes, a category of architecture view.

edges.cite: Clements et al., Documenting Software Architectures (C&C viewtype)
edges.note: The C&C view is the runtime-structure viewtype, a category of architecture view.

edges.cite: Clements et al., Documenting Software Architectures (allocation viewtype)
edges.note: The allocation view is the environment-mapping viewtype, a category of architecture view.
Allocation views map software elements from module (and C&C) views onto environmental structures.

edges.cite: Taylor, Medvidovic & Dashofy, Software Architecture (ADLs model components + connectors)
edges.note: ADLs formalize C&C structures, making components and connectors first-class constructs.
An ADL supplies the notation/conventions that constitute one or more model kinds.
ADLs incorporate interface specifications; several embed or build on an IDL for component ports.

edges.cite: CORBA/gRPC RPC model (stubs/skeletons generated from IDL)
edges.note: RPC/method-invocation connectors are defined by an IDL contract that generates stubs and skeletons.

edges.cite: AUTOSAR VFB specification (port interfaces)
edges.note: VFB ports are typed by AUTOSAR port interfaces that generate the RTE glue code.

edges.cite: AUTOSAR RTE specification (intra-ECU communication)
edges.note: The RTE maps intra-ECU port communication onto direct procedure calls between SW-Cs.

edges.cite: AUTOSAR VFB spec (sender-receiver, IS_QUEUED event semantics)
edges.note: Sender-receiver ports with queued (event) semantics deliver occurrences to receivers as an event connector.
Inter-ECU VFB signals are mapped onto the vehicle network, often a time-triggered bus (FlexRay).

edges.cite: Mehta, Medvidovic & Phadke, 'Towards a Taxonomy of Software Connectors' (ICSE 2000)
edges.note: Distributor connectors never act alone; they combine with procedure-call connectors (e.g. RPC).

edges.cite: Mehta, Medvidovic & Phadke, 'Towards a Taxonomy of Software Connectors' (ICSE 2000)
edges.note: Distributors augment stream connectors to route data among distributed endpoints.
Event delivery to registered subscribers relies on a distributor for routing/multicast.
Arbitrators mediate control (locks, scheduling) among components that interact via procedure calls.
Concurrency-control arbitration (locks, semaphores) guards shared data-access interactions.

edges.cite: Mehta, Medvidovic & Phadke 2000 (load balancing listed as an arbitrator service)
edges.note: Load balancing is an arbitrator function: redirecting requests among interchangeable components.

edges.cite: Mehta, Medvidovic & Phadke 2000 (linkage establishes channels used by other connectors)
edges.note: Linkage binds names/imports at build/load time so procedure-call connectors can act at runtime.
Both establish component associations: linkage binds at compile/load time, distributor via runtime lookup.
Linkage-established bindings enable event connectors to resolve producers/observers at runtime.

edges.cite: Mehta, Medvidovic & Phadke 2000 (pipe classified as a stream connector)
edges.note: Pipes-and-filters connects filters through pipes, which are stream connectors.
Implicit invocation transfers control by announcing events over event connectors.
Publish-subscribe delivers notifications from publishers to subscribers via event connectors.
An event-driven architecture transports occurrences from producers to consumers over event connectors.
Components in a shared-data style read/write the central store through data-access connectors.

edges.cite: Mehta, Medvidovic & Phadke 2000 (RPC = procedure call composed with distributor)
edges.note: The RPC style is built on the procedure-call connector extended for remote invocation.

edges.cite: Hohpe & Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns (ESB as messaging backbone)
edges.note: An ESB is layered over messaging: applications exchange messages through channels on the bus.
ESBs perform protocol bridging and message transformation, i.e. adaptor/converter functions.
ESBs provide content-based routing, a distributor/routing service between applications.
An ESB is an enriched message bus adding routing, transformation and orchestration.
Event notifications are commonly delivered as messages carried over message channels.

edges.cite: Hohpe & Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns (Message Channel)
edges.note: The messaging integration style connects applications through named message channels.

edges.cite: Hohpe & Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns (Datatype Channel)
edges.note: A Datatype Channel is a Message Channel that carries messages of only one data type.

edges.cite: Hohpe & Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns (Message Router)
edges.note: A Message Router consumes from one channel and republishes each message to a chosen output channel.
A secure channel realizes confidentiality by applying the Encrypt Data tactic to the transport.
A TLS/mTLS secure channel is a stream/transport connector hardened with encryption and auth.
mTLS secure channels commonly carry and authenticate remote procedure-call traffic.
An anti-corruption layer is built from adapters/translators that convert between models.
A Channel Adapter is an adaptor connector wrapping an application to a messaging channel.
Data-access connectors often embed translation/conversion, an adaptor role over the store's format.

edges.cite: Kopetz, Time-Triggered Architecture (temporal firewall interfaces)
edges.note: A temporal firewall's state data is deposited/read at predefined instants via time-triggered comms.

edges.cite: Kopetz, Real-Time Systems (state messages vs event messages)
edges.note: State-message firewall interfaces contrast with event-message connectors: overwrite vs queue/consume.
A temporal firewall is a non-consuming shared-memory read interface, a data-access-style connector.

edges.cite: Kopetz, Real-Time Systems (time-triggered vs event-triggered communication)
edges.note: TDMA time-triggered messaging contrasts with event-triggered notification as the core Kopetz dichotomy.

edges.cite: Kopetz & Bauer, The Time-Triggered Architecture (Proc. IEEE 2003)
edges.note: TTA's inter-node communication is a TDMA-scheduled time-triggered broadcast bus (TTP/C).

edges.cite: Evans, Domain-Driven Design (Context Map)
edges.note: A context map documents the system's bounded contexts and the relationships at their seams.

edges.cite: Evans, Domain-Driven Design (Context Map relationship patterns)
edges.note: Anti-Corruption Layer is one of the seam relationship types recorded on a context map.
A context map is a documented view of bounded contexts and their integration relationships.
Connectors like procedure-call are first-class elements populating a C&C view's runtime structures.
